definition: Managing the risk that a model, dataset, plugin or dependency an AI system relies on has been tampered with or compromised.
details: Modern AI applications assemble third-party models, weights, datasets, prompts and MCP tools; any of those links can carry backdoors, poisoned data or malicious code. Supply-chain controls track provenance, pin versions, scan artifacts and verify integrity before anything reaches production.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. The idea is simple: before something powerful is let loose, someone checks that it will not do real harm to real people. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. That deliberate caution is AI Supply Chain Security.
